name: Crizac Ltd
title: Crizac Ltd - 544439 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Crizac is an asset-light student-recruitment platform with strong FY26 growth (revenue +22.7%, PAT +41%), but FY27 guidance was withheld amid geopolitical uncertainty and margin gains were partly FX-driven.

summary.headline: Crizac FY26 revenue rose 22.7% to INR 10,422 mn and Q4 PAT rose 50% to INR 750 mn, but management withheld FY27 guidance until next quarter.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,917 mn (up 15% YoY, up 40.6% QoQ) and FY26 EBITDA reached about INR 2,824 mn with margin up 172 bps to 27%. Q4 EBITDA grew 42.8% YoY to INR 939 mn, with margin at 24%, and management attributed part of the Q4 margin jump to favourable GBP/INR movement it called transitional. Management completed or operationalised four acquisitions/investments (StudiesPlanet, 51% of Global Tree Careers, EduMentor commitment, Medway NZ team) and the company remains debt-free with net cash of INR 4,674 mn. FY27 guidance was deferred to the next quarter citing geopolitical uncertainty, with management saying growth should be in line with the past trend and a full-year growth of 15% to 17% noted in Q&A.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow to EBITDA FY26
financial_highlights.change: Affected by termination fee of about INR 55 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin FY26 (as cited in Q&A)

segments.name: Source markets (applications and conversion)
segments.commentary: Applications grew 43% YoY to about 394,000 and active agents rose 36% to 5,389; blended conversion about 14%, with India about 10%, China and LatAm about 20%, and Africa about 5%. Non-India source countries now contribute more than 50% of students.

segments.name: Destination markets
segments.commentary: UK is about 97% of destination mix per Q&A; management targets UK below 60% and rest of world about 40% in roughly two to three years, dependent on government policy. New Zealand was operationalised in April 2026 via the Medway team; Australia contracts are starting and recruitment expected within 3 to 6 months.

segments.name: Enrolments
segments.commentary: Student enrolments grew 14% YoY in FY26; management said it has grown 10% to 20% annually and expects similar or higher growth going forward.

guidance_outlook: No firm FY27 revenue guidance; management will issue guidance in the next quarter once geopolitical visibility improves.

Management said FY27 growth should be in line with the historical year-on-year rate; in Q&A the CFO said full-year growth of 15% to 17% is expected, and an analyst cited a 15% to 20% growth figure from earlier in the call.
Gross margin for the business to stay in a 20% to 30% range; analyst-cited FY27 gross margin of 28% to 30% was not explicitly rejected, and EBITDA margin guidance was withheld.
Visibility is roughly 6 to 9 months; management expects FY27 seasonality to match FY26, with H2 higher than H1.
Dividend payout of about 64% in Q4 FY26 is above the earlier committed 40%; management said it would consider buybacks versus dividends.
Australia recruitment expected to start within 3 to 6 months; management says 40% non-UK share is a three-year aspiration subject to immigration rules.
capex_capacity: Four transactions in FY26: StudiesPlanet acquisition (completed October 2025, opens LATAM corridor), 51% stake in Global Tree Careers (January 2026, B2C counselling and immigration), USD 2.5 mn over five years committed to EduMentor AI platform (March 2026), and onboarding of the Medway Educational Consultant team for New Zealand (April 2026).
Inorganic pipeline described as active across existing and new geographies; no specific deal values were disclosed for pipeline.
Company is asset-light; ROCE of 48.6% cited, and management said cash generation exceeds growth investment needs.
Over 300 US universities tied up per management, with Australia and Canada opening dependent on government policy.
demand_pricing: Management attributes the enrolment gap versus application growth to mix shift across markets with differing conversion rates.
Middle East pipeline damaged by the West Asia conflict; management expects it to recover as the war subsides.
US visa appointments limited; management ranks Australia ahead of the US as the next growth driver.
Pricing power argued to rise as UK Agent Quality Framework and Australian national codes raise compliance barriers; universities expected to consolidate suppliers.

FX: GBP/INR averaged 116 in FY26 vs 105 in FY25; management said 67% to 70% of expenses (agent commissions) are paid in GBP directly to agents, so FX impact is mainly on the portion repatriated to India.
Management quantified the FX-led benefit to EBITDA/gross margin at roughly 1% to 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why does application growth (43%) far exceed enrolment growth (14%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix shift: conversion varies by market (India about 10%, China/LatAm about 20%, Africa about 5%); blended conversion about 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Growth split between existing and new agents?
qa_highlights.answer: Not quantifiable on an agent-by-agent basis; active agents grew from about 4,000 to 5,500 and no agents were lost.

qa_highlights.question: Enrolment growth outlook in absolute terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been 10% to 20% a year; management expects similar or higher going forward, with FY26 at 14%.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance and expected growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred firm guidance to next quarter; full-year growth expected at 15% to 17%, and a 15% to 20% figure was referenced by an analyst.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 gross and EBITDA margins on a normalised basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin said to stay in the 20% to 30% range; analyst-quoted 28% to 30% for FY27 not rejected. EBITDA guidance withheld until growth guidance is given.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter holding and buyback versus dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding about 80% with two more years to reach the 75% SEBI threshold; management open to buybacks as a shareholder-value option.

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption (West Asia conflict) damaging the Middle East pipeline and delaying FY27 visibility.
UK concentration of about 97% of destination mix; policy changes (UK graduate visa cut from 24 to 18 months from January 2027) could affect demand.
Q4 margin partly driven by GBP strength, which management called transitional and expected to even out.
Australia and US entry dependent on university contracts and government visa rules; timing uncertain.
Cash conversion at 56% of EBITDA in FY26, affected by a termination fee of about INR 55 crore.
FY27 guidance to be issued in Q1 FY27 results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural demand, balance sheet and FY26 execution, but cautious and evasive on FY27 numbers, repeatedly deferring firm guidance and EBITDA margin estimates until the next quarter due to geopolitical uncertainty.
key_quotes: What I can say with confidence is structural demand for international education remains intact.

We believe we have already done most of the work. We have started getting some of the contracts from Australia and we believe over the next three to six months, we should be able to start recruiting and become a reasonable recruiter for all the Australian institutions.
Our platform is scaling, our balance sheet is strong, and our inorganic pipeline is active.
It can be roughly 1%-1.5% because of that.

growth.why: Management deferred firm FY27 guidance to next quarter, but in Q&A the CFO cited 15% to 17% full-year growth and enrolment growth of 10-20% held; backing is mainly application growth, new markets and mix, with no specific capacity or contracted orders quantified.
